heading: Networks can memorize random labels and generalize from natural labels
definition: the same architectures and training recipes that fit fixed random labels almost perfectly also reach held-out accuracy far above chance on the natural labels, while with random labels held-out accuracy stays at chance (small Inception, AlexNet and MLPs on CIFAR-10 without explicit regularization; Inception V3 on ImageNet, whose random-label fit is incomplete; Zhang et al. 2017).
summary: Independent studies support networks’ ability both to memorize random labels and to generalize from natural labels in small-model settings, though their setups vary. In comparisons using both label types, random-label test accuracy is near chance.

suggested_status.by_scale: Size not stated in counts: R2 for the small image/tabular model settings. 1-10B: ? for the full V1 conjunction; R0 for qualitative coexistence of random-answer fitting and retained pretrained QA behavior. versions.V1.studies_by_size lists no 10-100B or >100B coverage.
suggested_status.reason: The paired small-Inception result in arXiv:2306.10947#R1 and arXiv:2306.10947#R2 closely reproduces the named CIFAR-10 setting; arXiv:1802.05296#R2 and arXiv:1802.05296#R3 supply a regularized AlexNet comparison. arXiv:2207.09408#R1 and arXiv:2207.09408#R2 supply a paired infinite-width two-layer fully connected ReLU extension on EuroSAT; Table 2 does not identify the class pair. These support R2 for coexistence in the specified successful-fitting regimes. counts: versions.V1.verdicts.supports.studies = 63, versions.V1.studies_with_limits_scope = 13, and versions.V1.studies_with_challenges = 0; these totals include partial evidence and do not themselves establish independence. versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.evaluation.by_size identify the 1-10B coverage, where arXiv:2406.17642#R1 and arXiv:2406.17642#R2 provide qualitative retained QA behavior rather than the complete chance-referenced comparison.
suggested_status.open_questions: An independent matched Inception V3/ImageNet replication would strengthen the original larger-image setting. Complete quantitative natural-answer versus random-answer comparisons at language-model scales, separating pretrained retention from newly learned generalization, would change the scale-specific assessment. Resolving publication identities and missing endpoint rows would clarify the independent evidence base.

source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

original_result.setup: They trained Inception and MLP 3x512 on CIFAR-10 with natural or fixed random labels, without random cropping or weight decay.
original_result.result: Inception reached 100% training accuracy with either label set, but test accuracy was 85.75% with natural labels and 9.78% with random labels, near the 10% chance baseline. MLP 3x512 also reached 100% training accuracy with either label set, with test accuracy of 52.39% on natural labels and 10.48% on random labels.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An independent matched replication of the Inception V3/ImageNet comparison, including its incomplete random-label fit.
untested.basis: The original and CACM account describe the same experiment; other ImageNet rows concern different architectures, incomplete held-out measurements or training top-5 accuracy. counts: versions.V1.original_sources_linked identifies the original; versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.training and versions.V1.studies_by_size do not resolve architecture-specific replication.

untested.what: A quantitative, chance-referenced full V1 comparison for pretrained language-model QA, distinguishing newly learned generalization from retained pretrained knowledge; extension to larger listed scale categories.
untested.basis: The QA rows establish random-answer training loss and qualitative retention on unrelated questions. counts: versions.V1.studies_by_size and versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.evaluation.by_size contain 1-10B coverage but no 10-100B or >100B entries; the observed evaluation state does not establish the complete conjunction.

untested.what: The complete matched classifier-accuracy comparison for augmentation-based benign memorization.
untested.basis: The study's untested-parts line leaves the matched natural-label classifier comparison unreported; its principal clean-label outcome is K-NN probing of embeddings. counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation and versions.V1.rows_by_role do not distinguish probe accuracy from the trained classifier's accuracy.

untested.what: Whether longer training removes incomplete random-label fitting under the reported normalization and small-model protocols.
untested.basis: The normalization record explicitly leaves longer-training persistence untested; the small classical models lack extracted endpoints, and sigmoid noise-fitting convergence and budgets are unspecified. counts: versions.V1.coverage_by_operation.training.by_state records conditional outcomes without a convergence or training-budget breakdown.

wording_issues.issue: Use approximate chance for finite empirical measurements. Original CIFAR-10 random-label test accuracies include 9.78%, 10.48% and 10.61% against 10%. Bioresponse's 0.478 accuracy fraction is compared with uniform guessing at 0.5, while its class-frequency baseline is unreported.

wording_issues.phrase: the same architectures and training recipes
wording_issues.issue: Some extensions change training duration, target scale, initialization history or trainable layers. The binary-MNIST preprint uses 20 natural-label versus 120 random-label epochs; margin control uses label-dependent target scales; activation-pattern memorization can start from natural-label weights or freeze layers.

wording_issues.phrase: fit fixed random labels almost perfectly
wording_issues.issue: This cannot be generalized to every architecture or recipe. WideResNet-28-10 after 50 epochs with weight decay has random-label training error 17.24% under Spectral normalization and 29.04% under Stable-30, versus 1.22% for Vanilla; Vanilla is not an incomplete-fit case. For CIFAR-10 WRN-28-10 without explicit regularization at l-infinity budget 8/255, PGD-AT fails to converge on random labels, whereas TRADES nearly fits them; training results alone do not establish the held-out component. Activation-pattern CNN incomplete-fit limits apply to MNIST MemRetrainLast, FashionMNIST MemRetrainLast widths 64/128, MNIST MemRandomLast width 64, and FashionMNIST MemRandomLast widths 64/128. FashionMNIST frozen-layer widths 256/512 instead nearly fit. Narrow models and multi-step schedules also limit extensions. These are conditional extension limits rather than failed replications of the named original settings.

Partial-corruption experiments demonstrate noisy-example memorization alongside clean-task generalization within one dataset. They do not establish the matched natural-label versus entirely random-label comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: while with random labels held-out accuracy stays at chance
wording_issues.issue: Several supporting verdicts establish memorization and natural-label generalization without measuring the random-label held-out endpoint. High test error, unreadable curves, or introductory statements attributed to prior work do not independently establish chance performance.

Keep accuracy distinct from loss, training top-5 accuracy, embedding-probe accuracy and qualitative answer retention. Random-feature models can remain at chance accuracy while test loss changes; ImageNet capacity evidence using training top-5 does not establish held-out top-1 performance. Llama 3 8B reaches near-zero training loss after 100 epochs under both true-answer and randomized-answer fine-tuning; this training comparison and qualitative QA retention do not supply a random-target held-out chance comparison.

wording_issues.phrase: Inception V3 on ImageNet, whose random-label fit is incomplete
wording_issues.issue: Preserve this exception. The original unregularized random-label Inception V3 experiment reports top-1 training accuracy 95.20% and top-1 test accuracy 0.11%, against a stated chance top-1 test-accuracy baseline of 0.1%. The CACM republication reports 95.20% and incomplete fitting, but does not directly report the 0.11% test result or explicitly bind 95.20% to the full no-augmentation/no-dropout/no-weight-decay condition; those details belong to the original appendix. The version does not claim perfect ImageNet fitting.

method_sensitivity.what: Shuffled-label fitting depends on model width and frozen representations. Corrected MNIST CNN MemRetrainLast training/validation accuracy is 18.36%/10.62% at width 128 and 56.22%/10.10% at width 512. On MNIST, the later record's MLP-64 reaches only 31.11% shuffled-label training accuracy under MemRetrainAll, which equals MemRetrainLast for MLPs; its CNN-512 reaches 100% under MemRetrainAll, with all layers retrained from natural-label trained weights.

method_sensitivity.factor: Normalization, training budget and learning-rate schedule
method_sensitivity.what: Under the same 50-epoch protocol with weight decay, WideResNet-28-10 random-label training error is 1.22% for Vanilla, 17.24% for Spectral and 29.04% for Stable-30. Vanilla shows near-perfect fitting; the normalized methods fit incompletely. ResNet-110 remains incompletely fitted under its low-learning-rate, 200-epoch protocol. VGG-11 fails under its multi-step schedule. The binary-MNIST preprint uses 120 random-label versus 20 natural-label epochs.

method_sensitivity.factor: Thermal noise, privacy and information regularization
method_sensitivity.what: Low-noise Entropy-SGD overfits random labels, but its cited row does not quantify the fitting endpoint; higher-noise recipes suppress memorization. Privacy-tuned Entropy-SGLD retains natural-label learning without random-label overfitting. MNIST SGLD random-label training error stays approximately 0.9 for inverse temperature τ < 10³; heavy overfitting begins when τ exceeds 50,000, the training-set size. Random-label true error remains approximately 0.9; near-perfect training fit is unquantified. DPSGD suppresses small-AlexNet noise memorization while retaining natural-data learning. On CIFAR-10, small AlexNet, All-CNN and ResNet completely fit random labels at low information-regularization β and underfit at higher β. These β-sweep rows and the Entropy-SGLD natural-label-only row cannot individually determine V1 coexistence.

For WRN-28-10 on CIFAR-10, PGD-AT and TRADES both achieve almost 100% natural and robust training accuracy on true labels. On random labels, PGD-AT fails to converge, whereas TRADES reaches nearly 100% training accuracy. Almost-perfect random-label fitting is absent for PGD-AT; these training measurements alone cannot determine full V1 coexistence. AlexNet experiments elsewhere report fitting under FGM, PGM and WRM with slight delays; their different architectures and adversarial conditions do not establish a matched conflict.

Random-label pretraining changes subsequent natural-label generalization. Vanilla-SGD ResNet18 reports 56.024% test accuracy after random-label pretraining versus 84.838% from random initialization; another no-weight-decay ResNet-18 reports 89.7% versus 90.0%. Their recipes differ, so these effect magnitudes are not interchangeable.

method_sensitivity.factor: Corruption fraction, available data and weight decay
method_sensitivity.what: For quadratic modular addition at data fraction 0.5 and corruption fraction 0.35, weight decay 0 permits near-perfect training and test accuracy; weight decay 5 permits only partial corrupted-label memorization; weight decay 15 retains generalization without corrupted-label memorization. Very high corruption or very little data instead permits near-perfect training accuracy with chance test accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Input construction, sample variance and dataset size
method_sensitivity.what: Adding input connections permits arbitrary-noise fitting where standard sigmoid and add-shortcuts networks fail. Low-variance toy-MNIST prevents noisy-label memorization, whereas σ² = 1 permits interpolation. Increasing random-label dataset size reduces fitting for the tested CIFAR-10 MLP and transformed-MNIST equivariant models.

method_sensitivity.factor: SGD noise, corruption level and training stage
method_sensitivity.what: After memorizing partially randomized MNIST labels, larger learning-rate-to-batch-size ratios improve held-out generalization, depending on momentum and corruption. Early-stopped versus interpolating ResNets have different noise profiles; Figure 7 uses n = 9k, 18k, 36k and 70k. VGG16 on CIFAR-100 with 50% randomized labels fits permuted examples later and eventually shows declining test accuracy. The paper claims no weight decay or other regularization, but its VGG16 architecture lists BatchNorm and Dropout. Training-subset fitting alone cannot establish V1 coexistence. Binary-MNIST FC-600-2 generalization gaps are 0.014, 0.077, 0.167 and 0.263 at random-label fractions 0.0, 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6; Figure S-16 does not supply separate training/test errors.

Global backpropagation memorizes random labels better than greedy local training in CIFAR-10 ResNet18, although absolute random-label fitting endpoints are unavailable. Corrected natural-label annotations are approximately 99% training and 91% test accuracy for backpropagation versus approximately 98% training and 88% test accuracy for fully greedy training.

The MNIST margin-control comparisons change target scales between label conditions and compare unconstrained full-batch gradient descent with Frobenius-constrained Nero. Their paired results therefore require these recipe qualifications; the natural-label 81% versus 88% discrepancy is internal to the study.
